description: The engine's ClassDB, with the classes the project's scripts declare beside it: find classes, read one in full, or walk an inheritance tree. The project's classes are read from the scripts on disk, so one written a moment ago is there before any scan. query and inheritance answer them under project_classes, project_children and project_descendants, each with its path, what it extends and whether it is abstract; info reads engine classes only, and a project class is read in full by script_info structure. Operations: query: classes matching a filter or category, the engine's and the project's; info (needs className): methods, properties, signals and enums of one class, or one member of it by name; inheritance (needs className): ancestors and descendants of one class, an engine class or one a project script declares. Default query.

category.description: query: limit to one family. Only for op query.

className.description: info, inheritance: the class. Only for ops info, inheritance.

filter.description: query: a substring of the class name. Only for op query.

includeInherited.description: info: also name every member the class inherits, under inherited: one entry per ancestor, nearest first, with the names of the methods, properties, signals and enums it declares. The class's own members stay in full; member reads any inherited one in full. Default false. Only for op info.

instantiableOnly.description: query: leave out abstract classes: an engine class that cannot be instantiated, and a project class that is @abstract or built on an engine class that cannot be. A class extending an @abstract one is kept. Default false. Only for op query.

member.description: info: one member by name, a method, property, signal, enum or constant, with its signature and which class declares it, looked for on the class and every ancestor. The whole of Control is seventy thousand characters; the question "does this engine have it, and what does it take" is this. A name nothing declares is refused with the members whose names contain it. Only for op info.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the project directory, the one holding project.godot.
